title: Clarify screenShake randSign construction-time behavior
description:
## Background

`screenShake(near:)` in `GameScene.swift` (~line 674-680) defines a local closure `randSign` that returns +1 or -1 randomly. It calls `randSign()` four times inline while constructing an `SKAction.sequence([...])` literal. Those four calls execute at **construction time**, once per call to `screenShake`. The resulting offsets are baked into the action.

Effect: each shake gets a fresh random pattern (different shakes look different from each other), but the four "wobble" beats inside one shake are not independently random — they're a single random pattern that plays back identically during that one shake.

Fine for the visual goal. The code just reads like it intends per-frame randomness; the indirection through `randSign` is misleading.

## Fix (pick one)

**Option A — add a tombstone comment (smaller diff, recommended):**
```swift
// randSign() is called four times at construction time, producing a
// fresh-but-then-fixed random pattern per shake. Not per-frame random.
let randSign: () -> CGFloat = { Bool.random() ? 1 : -1 }
```

**Option B — make the per-shake randomness explicit by extracting variables:**
```swift
let s1: CGFloat = Bool.random() ? 1 : -1
let s2: CGFloat = Bool.random() ? 1 : -1
let s3: CGFloat = Bool.random() ? 1 : -1
let s4: CGFloat = Bool.random() ? 1 : -1
let shake = SKAction.sequence([
    .moveBy(x: amp * s1, y: -amp * 0.5 * s2, duration: 0.04),
    ...
])
```

## Acceptance

A reader can tell at a glance whether randomness is per-shake or per-frame, without running the code.

## Files

- PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift (~lines 674-680). After Bead #6, lives in IcicleSystem.
close_reason: Added a 7-line tombstone comment above the randSign closure in screenShake() (GameScene.swift ~line 734) explaining that randSign() is called at SKAction construction time, not on each playback frame — so each shake builds a fresh random wobble pattern that then plays back identically. Intent is now self-documenting.

title: fix(lifecycle): score balloons after screen lock — reset dt anchor + pause on resign
description:
## Symptom
Lock the screen mid-round, unlock 30 s later → score jumps by hundreds and icicle physics teleports. Player reports it as cheating-looking score inflation.

## Root cause
`GameScene.update(_:)` (PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift) computes `dt = currentTime - lastUpdateTime` and adds it to `elapsed`. `score = Int(elapsed * 10)`. When the screen locks the display link halts, but `lastUpdateTime` is frozen at its pre-lock value. On wake, the first `update(_:)` runs with `currentTime` advanced by the lock duration → `dt ≈ lock_duration`, `elapsed` jumps minutes, score balloons, and `penguin.update(dt:)` / `icicles.update(dt:)` integrate one giant step.

`lastUpdateTime = 0` is already the sentinel that produces `dt = 0` on the next frame (see closed penguinslide-jj2 which fixed the equivalent issue for restart/start transitions). Need the same reset on app foregrounding.

## Acceptance
1. Lock screen during active play for >= 30 s. On unlock, score has not jumped by more than ~1-2 s worth of progression (<= 20 points), and no icicles have teleported.
2. The same holds if the lock happens during the start prompt or game-over overlay (no spurious state changes).
3. Notification observers are added in didMove(to:) and removed in willMove(from:) — no leaks across scene reloads.
4. Both Debug and Release builds compile clean.

## Implementation sketch
- Observe UIApplication.willResignActiveNotification → set view?.isPaused = true (defense in depth)
- Observe UIApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification → set lastUpdateTime = 0 (the key fix), then view?.isPaused = false
- removeObserver in willMove(from:)

## Files
- PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift

## Out of scope
- Adding a proper in-game pause UI / menu — separate bead if wanted.
- Auto-trigger game-over on background — discuss before implementing; not obviously the right behavior.

## Related
- penguinslide-jj2 (closed) — same sentinel pattern was applied to restart/start transitions.
close_reason: Added observeAppLifecycle() invoked from didMove(to:): registers willResignActiveNotification (pauses view) and didBecomeActiveNotification (resets lastUpdateTime = 0 — triggering the existing dt-skip sentinel in update(_:) — then unpauses view). removeObserver in willMove(from:). Debug + Release both BUILD SUCCEEDED. Manual on-device/sim lock-screen verification (acceptance #1/#2) left to user since automating lock-screen via xcrun isn't available locally; logic mirrors closed penguinslide-jj2's restart-time anchor reset, so the regression class is collapsed.

title: Snowball impact rework: replace box-rendering burst sheet with icicle-style gravity snow chunks + puff + regenerated splat SFX
description:
# Snowball Impact Rework — kill the box, shatter like icicles

Date: 2026-06-12 · Author: VioletPlateau (with Mina's device feedback) · Status: approved-by-feedback, implementing

## Problem (observed on device by Mina)

Snowball impacts (on Papi and at the near plane) render as a **white square**
with faint art inside, and don't read as an animation at all.

**Root cause (verified by inspecting the asset):** the SpriteCook sheet
`snowball_impact_burst.png` has an opaque white background baked into all 8
frames (alpha channel present but background not transparent), and frames 6–8
are nearly blank white rectangles. `EncounterFX.playHitBurst` animates the
sheet correctly — every frame is just a white card. No code bug; bad asset.

## Decision

Replace the sheet-based burst with the **icicle-shatter recipe** (Mina's
explicit spec: "like the icicles bursting … follows gravity … has a noise"):

1. **Gravity snow chunks** — on every resolved hit, spawn 6–10 small rounded
   snow-chip sprites (cached texture, never SKShapeNode-per-particle) launched
   radially with upward bias, integrated manually (`vy -= g·dt`) in a new
   `EncounterFX.update(dt:)` ticked from the encounter phase bodies. dt == 0
   sentinel = no-op; game-over freeze = ticks stop = coherent frozen frame;
   `reset()` scrubs. Sized/launched × the avatar depth scale. Fade by lifetime
   fraction in the same tick (no SKActions for shards).
2. **Powder puff** — one soft cached radial puff at the impact point
   (scale-up + fade via tracked one-shot SKAction, pause-registered), so the
   chunk burst has a core. Absorbed (i-frame) hits: fewer chunks, dimmer puff,
   same as the icicle "softer pop".
3. **Sound** — keep the existing `snowball_impact.caf` trigger (already wired
   in SnowMonsterEncounterSystem); regenerate the sample via ElevenLabs
   (`/sound-effects`): wet snow splat + icy crunch, punchy, < 1 s.
4. **Remove the sheet path** — delete `SnowballBurst.imageset`, the
   `Sprite.snowballBurst` case, `EncounterAnimations.snowballBurst*`, and the
   burst-sheet knobs; mark the manifest entry retired (history kept). Update
   EncounterFXTests / animation tests accordingly.
5. **NOT regenerating a burst sheet via SpriteCook** — the box came from a
   generated sheet; procedural chunks match the icicle FX exactly and cannot
   have background artifacts. (Revisit only if Mina wants a fancier core
   splash after feeling this version.)

## Non-goals

- Catch-the-snowball mechanic: separate design decision, asked to Mina.
- Encounter pacing/ground: shipped earlier (fr7/hhz), awaiting device sign-off.

## Verification

Simulator embargo still on → compile gate (`xcodebuild build-for-testing`,
generic destination) + pure-logic unit tests compile; runtime suites deferred
to `penguinslide-x06`; feel sign-off by Mina on device.
close_reason: Impact rework: retired opaque-background SpriteCook burst sheet (rendered as white box); replaced with icicle-style procedural FX — powder puff + 6-10 gravity-integrated snow chunks ticked from encounter phase bodies; derived lateralHitRadius from Papi body + ball core (38pt -> ~80pt, fixes shoulder hits scoring as +n dodges); fresh ElevenLabs splat sample. Compile gate green; runtime verification deferred to penguinslide-x06

title: fix: monster mode trigger stalls game, never enters encounter
description:
USER BUG: arming Snow Monster Mode (settings, gyu.30) drastically slowed/stalled the game and never showed monster mode; later evidence: instant game-over on entry, no Papi visible.

ROOT CAUSE (two mechanisms, both verified in sim):
1. STALL: the gyu.30 trigger seam itself is correct (pendingEncounterStart consumed exactly once, single transition). But updateEncounterIntro/Outro were inert no-ops and nothing advanced encounterIntro -> encounter -> normal (bead .17 unlanded), so entry parked the game in a no-op phase: penguin/icicle integration stopped, tilt ignored, icicles hung mid-air = perceived drastic slowdown/freeze.
2. INSTANT GAME-OVER: falling icicles are physics-velocity-driven (IcicleSystem writes body.velocity); when phase leaves .normal their velocity keeps integrating (physicsWorld.speed stays 1; hidden/paused nodes still simulate) and didBegin was not phase-gated -> in-flight icicles coast through the penguin at entry -> tryTakeHit -> triggerGameOver.

FIX (GameScene.swift only):
- beginEncounterPresentation(): icicles.reset() (clears in-flight icicles/shadows/shards/bursts + their SKActions), hide+pause worldRoot, show+unpause encounterRoot with INTERIM world (mountain backdrop, perspective ground, monster idle loop, papi rear-slide placeholder, SNOW MONSTER! banner).
- didBegin gated on phase == .normal: encounter damage can never arrive via the 2D contact pass (KTD3 doctrine); interim encounter has no death path.
- updateEncounterIntro/Outro: phaseTime-driven crossfades (manual dt integration, no SKActions) honoring Tuning.Encounter.intro/outroDuration; stub SnowMonsterEncounterSystem runs a 6 s interim 'encounter running' timer then routes encounter -> outro.
- endEncounterPresentation(): idempotent restore (removeAllChildren on encounterRoot, unhide/unpause worldRoot, encounterSystem.reset()); also called from restart() so death/restart mid-encounter restores the side view.
- dt==0 sentinel: every hop goes through transition(to:), once per transition.
- DEBUG: encounterState SKLabelNode (phase + worldRoot/encounterRoot child counts) for tests.

VERIFIED: 4 enter/exit cycles in sim incl. arming with icicles mid-air (no game-over) and debug-forced game-over mid-encounter (Play Again restores side view). Node counts stable across cycles (w=13 baseline, e=0 after every exit; transient +5 snow puffs self-remove). test-unit 53/53 green, test-xcui 4/4 green.

INTERIM bridge is clearly commented; beads gyu.10-.17 replace the bodies, not the seams.

title: Group Tuning into nested namespaces (Penguin/Icicle/Chase/Feel/Run)
description:
## Background

The `Tuning` enum holds 27 flat constants with MARK comments providing visual-only grouping. Reading `Tuning.gravityScaleStart` vs `Tuning.tiltCurve` gives no hint that one's an icicle physics knob and the other's a penguin input curve. README's difficulty table already groups them by subsystem — code should match.

## Proposed structure

```swift
enum Tuning {
    enum Penguin {
        static let maxSpeed: CGFloat = 720
        static let tiltCurve: CGFloat = 1.5
        static let collisionRadiusFraction: CGFloat = 0.30
        static let tiltResponseRate: CGFloat = 5.0
        static let iceDecayRate: CGFloat = 0.7
        static let leanMaxAngle: CGFloat = 0.30
        static let leanStiffness: CGFloat = 60
        static let leanDampingRatio: CGFloat = 0.55   // (updated naming per current README)
    }

    enum Icicle {
        static let warningDuration: TimeInterval = 0.75
        static let spawnIntervalStart: TimeInterval = 1.10
        static let spawnIntervalEnd:   TimeInterval = 0.34
        static let sceneGravity: CGFloat = 700
        static let gravityScaleStart: CGFloat = 0.45
        static let gravityScaleEnd: CGFloat = 1.10
        static let gravityScaleVariance: CGFloat = 0.20
        static let initialDownVelocity: CGFloat = 50
    }

    enum Chase {
        static let leadFactor: CGFloat = 0.4
        static let jitterStart: CGFloat = 0.35
        static let jitterEnd: CGFloat = 0.10
        static let randomChance: Double = 0.20
    }

    enum Feel {
        static let shardCount: Int = 6
        static let shardLaunchSpeed: CGFloat = 220
        static let shardLifetime: TimeInterval = 0.6
        static let shakePeakAmplitude: CGFloat = 8

    }

    enum Run {
        static let rampDuration: TimeInterval = 90.0
        static let gracePeriod: TimeInterval = 1.2
        static let playWidthFraction: CGFloat = 0.62
    }
}
```

Update every reference. After Bead penguinslide-6 (extraction), each subsystem mostly touches one sub-enum which is even cleaner.

## Acceptance
1. Tuning enum structure mirrors README sections.
2. All call sites updated. Compile clean.
3. README difficulty table updated to use full paths (e.g., `Tuning.Penguin.maxSpeed`).

- README.md — update difficulty table column names

Updated 31 references across Penguin.swift, IcicleSystem.swift, GameScene.swift via a single sed pass. title: Snow Monster boss encounter mode (Papi Penguin pseudo-3D dodge sequence)
description:
EPIC. Plan: docs/plans/2026-06-10-001-feat-snow-monster-encounter-plan.md (beads are self-contained; the doc is reference only).

GOAL: At random points during a normal run, the 2D side-view ice field transitions into a pseudo-3D behind-the-penguin boss encounter. The player character is branded Papi Penguin for this mode. A snowman-like snow monster in the mountains ahead throws snowballs toward the camera; the player dodges laterally, goalkeeper-style, using the exact same tilt input pipeline and feel as the normal game. Surviving the volley pays a score bonus and returns to the run; losing all hearts ends the run through the standard game-over flow.

KEY DECISIONS (made at plan time):
- Faux-3D is pure SpriteKit scale-over-depth via a DepthProjector (screenScale = focal/(focal+z), y rises toward a horizon line, x converges to a vanishing point). title: GamePhase state machine in GameScene: normal/encounterIntro/encounter/encounterOutro with dt-sentinel-owning transition(to:)
description:
BACKGROUND: GameScene.update currently has one body: combo decay, penguin.update(dt:tilt:), icicles.update(dt:elapsed:), score drip - all behind the guard (isStarted, not isGameOver). WORK: Add a private GamePhase enum (normal, encounterIntro, encounter, encounterOutro) and a phase var to GameScene (PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift). Keep the existing dt computation and the isStarted/!isGameOver guard EXACTLY as-is at the top of update(_:). Inside the guard, switch on phase: .normal runs the current body unchanged; .encounter calls only encounterSystem.update(dt:tilt:currentTilt()); .encounterIntro/.encounterOutro tick transition timelines (timeline driving lands in the transition beads - here just the routing seams and no-op stubs). ACCEPTANCE:

- transition(to:) is the sole writer of phase, and provably resets lastUpdateTime on every call.
- .encounter phase never calls icicles.update (no spawn-timer advancement).
- restart() restores phase .normal + encounter system reset.
- Update-ordering doc comment in update(_:) is extended to mention phase routing, keeping the contract text accurate.

title: Depth-based collision + dodge detection with severity scoring (manual, unit-tested)
description:
BACKGROUND: KTD3 - the encounter collision is fully manual. Per frame, inside SnowMonsterEncounterSystem.update (NOT didBegin - there are no physics bodies on snowballs): hit iff z < Tuning.Encounter.depthWindow AND |ball.worldX - papi.worldX| < lateralHitRadius; dodge iff the ball crosses z <= 0 unresolved. This extends the repo doctrine (physics is manual; bodies exist only where 2D contact detection actually works). Severity of a dodge = normalized lateral near-miss closeness, feeding the existing close-call bonus treatment so encounter scoring reuses the bonusPoints pipeline.

WORK: Implement collision/dodge resolution in SnowMonsterEncounterSystem with the math extracted into pure, static helper functions (testable without nodes): resolve(ball, papiWorldX) -> .none / .hit / .dodged(severity). Rules: a ball resolves EXACTLY once (resolved flag; a hit consumes the ball with impact FX; a dodge culls it after it exits the near plane); severity = max(0, 1 - lateralMiss/severityRadius) computed AT the crossing frame; hits route OUT via a callback the GameScene wires to penguin.tryTakeHit (the system stays score/HP-agnostic exactly like IcicleSystem.onCloseCall keeps it score-agnostic); dodges route via onDodge(severity, screenPoint) for bonus + floatBonus display. After each resolution, decrement outstanding-ball accounting for the volley-completion bead.

FILES: PenguinSlide/Encounter/SnowMonsterEncounterSystem.swift, PenguinSlideTests/SnowballCollisionTests.swift (new).

UNIT TESTS (pure helpers, detailed messages):
- Ball entering depthWindow with lateral overlap resolves .hit exactly once across consecutive frames.
- Lateral miss at the window resolves .dodged at plane-crossing with severity proportional to closeness; far miss yields severity 0 but still resolves.
- Boundary cases: exactly at lateralHitRadius (define inclusive/exclusive, assert it), ball with drift entering the radius INSIDE the window mid-band (frame-stepped simulation catches it).
- Fast-ball tunneling guard: with max zSpeed and 30 fps dt, a ball cannot step across the entire depthWindow in one frame undetected - if knobs permit that, the resolver must use segment (previous-z to current-z) overlap, not point-in-band; test enforces whichever contract is chosen.
- Severity clamped to 0...1.

ACCEPTANCE: tests green; i-frame interaction documented (a hit during i-frames still consumes the ball with soft FX - mirror onIcicleHitPenguin accepted=false handling).

The severity radius for dodge scoring is a separate knob from lateralHitRadius (a dodge severity of 1.0 should require a genuinely close shave; if they share a knob, every dodge scores 0 because severity is measured AT the miss boundary). Add severityRadius to Tuning.Encounter via the knobs bead if not already present - coordinate.

title: Volley orchestration: throw scheduling, completion detection, encounter outcome callbacks
description:
BACKGROUND: An encounter is one volley: N snowballs thrown at a cadence, both lerped from run difficulty at trigger time (volleyCountStart/End etc. in Tuning.Encounter). The encounter ends in exactly one of two ways: all balls resolved with the penguin alive (WIN -> outro) or HP exhausted mid-volley (LOSS -> standard game over). SnowMonsterEncounterSystem is the orchestrator, mirroring IcicleSystem shape: owns monster + balls + world + avatar references, communicates outward only via callbacks.

WORK: In PenguinSlide/Encounter/SnowMonsterEncounterSystem.swift implement: begin(difficultyProgress:) computes the volley plan (count, interval, zSpeed) and starts the cycle; per-frame update drives monster telegraph(telegraphDuration) -> throw -> release-signal spawns the ball -> recover, repeating until count exhausted; onVolleyComplete fires only when the LAST ball RESOLVES (hit or dodge), not at the last throw - in-flight balls must finish. Callbacks out: onSnowballHit(worldX) (GameScene routes to penguin.tryTakeHit + checks isAlive -> triggerGameOver), onDodge(severity, point), onVolleyComplete. pauseActions() pauses any SKActions on encounter nodes (mirror pauseShardActions - called from triggerGameOver so a death freeze is total). reset() returns everything to a cold state (called from GameScene.restart and after outro).

- onVolleyComplete only after last resolution (unit-test the accounting with a scripted sequence).
- pauseActions() freezes all encounter visuals (manual check under forced game over).
- begin() after reset() yields a clean second encounter (idempotent re-entry).

title: EncounterTrigger: pure random-encounter scheduler with seeded-RNG unit tests
description:
BACKGROUND: Encounters fire at random points during a normal run (requirement R1) but must be deterministic under test and never fire at unfair moments. Pure scheduling math in its own type keeps GameScene small and makes the probability behavior unit-testable - the same separation IcicleSystem has from GameScene.

WORK: Create PenguinSlide/Encounter/EncounterTrigger.swift: a struct fed (dt, gameplayElapsed, eligible: Bool) per frame, returning a fire decision. Internals: armed only after Tuning.Encounter.minRunTime; enforces minSpacing since the last fire; caps fires at maxPerRun; accumulates fractional seconds and rolls perSecondChance once per whole second (NOT per frame - per-frame rolls make the effective probability framerate-dependent). RNG is injected (any RandomNumberGenerator, defaulting to SystemRandomNumberGenerator) so tests seed it. eligible is computed by the CALLER (GameScene): phase == .normal AND isStarted AND not isGameOver AND penguin not inside i-frames AND no icicle currently inside a danger window near the penguin (so the intro sweep never eats an icicle that was about to legitimately hit - fairness rule from the plan). reset() re-arms everything for restart().

UNIT TESTS (seeded RNG, detailed assertion messages):
- Never fires before minRunTime even with RNG forced to always-fire.
- After a fire, no fire until minSpacing has elapsed.
- maxPerRun cap holds over an arbitrarily long simulated run; reset() re-arms.
- Frame-rate independence: same seed + same simulated wall-clock yields the same fire times at 30 fps and 120 fps step sizes.
- eligible == false suppresses fires and does NOT advance the spacing/arming clocks incorrectly (define and assert which clocks advance while ineligible: arming time advances, the per-second roll is skipped).
- Statistical sanity: over a seeded 120 s simulation, fire count within expected tolerance for the configured perSecondChance.

title: DepthProjector: pseudo-3D projection math (pure, unit-tested)
description:
BACKGROUND: SpriteKit is 2D; the encounter fakes depth with single-vanishing-point perspective. One shared projector must position EVERYTHING (monster, snowballs, ground bands, lane markings, shadows) so all elements agree on the geometry - per-element ad-hoc scaling is how faux-3D scenes fall apart visually. This was the core technique decision (KTD1): scale-over-depth in pure SpriteKit, SceneKit overlay rejected (forks pause semantics, asset pipeline, and SKLabelNode test accessibility), SKTransformNode rejected as core (only tilts flat planes).

WORK: Create PenguinSlide/Encounter/DepthProjector.swift, a pure value type built from Tuning.Encounter geometry knobs + scene size. API sketch (directional): project(worldX:z:) -> (point: CGPoint, scale: CGFloat) where t = focal/(focal+z); screenX = vanishingX + (worldX - vanishingX)*t; screenY = horizonY - (horizonY - papiPlaneY)*t; scale = t. z=0 is the camera/Papi plane (scale 1.0), z=zMonster is the monster depth. Clamp z below 0 to 0 (a ball crossing the plane must never invert/explode). No SpriteKit node dependencies - takes and returns CG types only, so it is trivially unit-testable and reusable by the world builder, the snowball system, and the avatar placement.

FILES: PenguinSlide/Encounter/DepthProjector.swift (new), PenguinSlideTests/DepthProjectorTests.swift (new).

UNIT TESTS (detailed messages):
- z=0 yields scale 1.0 at papiPlaneY; z=zMonster yields focal/(focal+zMonster) at the expected y.
- Strict monotonicity of scale and screenY in z (sampled sweep); screenX converges toward vanishingX as z grows.
- Two worldX at equal z preserve order and proportional separation.
- z < 0 clamps to the z=0 projection; degenerate focal (0 or negative) is rejected or clamped safely - pick one, assert it.
- Resolution independence: normalized layout identical across two scene sizes.

title: Document gravity-integration / physics-pause ordering contract
description:
## Background

`update(_:)` in `GameScene.swift` has the structure:
1. Compute `dt`
2. Update `lastUpdateTime`
3. `guard isStarted, !isGameOver else { return }`
4. Movement, spawning, gravity integration, landing checks
5. Score update

When the penguin dies, `didBegin(_:)` (called from SpriteKit's contact resolution, which runs AFTER `update(_:)` in the same frame) sets `isGameOver = true` and `physicsWorld.speed = 0`. The next frame's `update(_:)` correctly early-returns, and `physicsWorld.speed = 0` halts SpriteKit's integration.

The latent issue: this ordering is implicit. If someone moves `integrateCustomGravity` and `checkIcicleLandings` OUTSIDE the `isStarted/!isGameOver` guard (e.g., to support a pause animation, or refactors update for clarity), one frame of post-death physics integration would occur.

## Fix (pick one)

**Option A — tombstone comment on update(_:):**
```swift
// IMPORTANT: All per-frame physics work must stay BEHIND the
// isStarted/!isGameOver guard. didBegin runs inside SpriteKit's
// physics step (AFTER update returns), so on the death frame we've
// already executed update(); we rely on the next frame's guard to
// halt further integration.
```

**Option B — restructure into a helper that no-ops when paused:**
```swift
override func update(_ currentTime: TimeInterval) {
    let dt = ...
    lastUpdateTime = currentTime
    runGameTick(dt: dt)
}

private func runGameTick(dt: TimeInterval) {
    guard isStarted, !isGameOver else { return }
    movePenguin(dt: dt, tilt: readTilt())
    maybeSpawn(dt: dt)
    integrateCustomGravity(dt: dt)
    checkIcicleLandings()
    score = Int(elapsed * 10)
}
```

Recommend Option B if Bead #6 (refactor) happens; Option A as a safety net otherwise.

## Acceptance

The dependency on guard-ordering is documented OR the structure makes the safety property local (a reader can verify it without reading the whole update loop).

## Files

PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift
close_reason: Added a docstring on update(_:) (GameScene.swift ~line 401) calling out the ordering contract: all per-frame physics work must stay behind the isStarted/!isGameOver guard, because didBegin runs INSIDE SpriteKit's physics step (after update returns) on the death frame. The next frame's guard plus physicsWorld.speed=0 halts motion. Also opportunistically cleaned up two stale doc comments at :190 and :495 that still referenced the old userData['gravity'] approach (replaced upstream by FallingBody) — they now reference integrateAndCheckLandings(dt:) and FallingBody entries respectively.

title: Make lastUpdateTime restart-safe
description:
## Background

`lastUpdateTime` is initialized to 0 at scene construction. The check `lastUpdateTime == 0 ? 0 : (currentTime - lastUpdateTime)` produces dt = 0 on the very first frame ever, then normal dt thereafter. The assignment `lastUpdateTime = currentTime` runs every frame BEFORE the isStarted/!isGameOver guard — meaning lastUpdateTime keeps ticking even when the rest of update bails. This is why dt stays small after a long pause: the timestamp is fresh.

Currently safe. But if a future refactor moves the `lastUpdateTime = currentTime` assignment INSIDE the guard (e.g., to consolidate "do nothing while paused"), then on game-over the timestamp would freeze, and on restart the next frame would compute a huge dt (could be 10s+) and the penguin would teleport.

## Fix (defensive)

Reset `lastUpdateTime = 0` in `restart()` and on the !isStarted → isStarted transition. The 0-sentinel in the ternary already handles this — restart effectively gets a "first frame" dt = 0, which is correct.

```swift
private func restart() {
    // ... existing reset ...
    lastUpdateTime = 0
}
```

```swift
override func touchesBegan(...) {
    if !isStarted {
        isStarted = true
        lastUpdateTime = 0
        ...
    }
}
```

## Acceptance

Even if a future refactor narrows the lastUpdateTime write to inside the guard, restart and start don't produce a teleport.

## Files

PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift
close_reason: Added lastUpdateTime = 0 resets in both restart() (after leanVelocity reset) and the !isStarted→isStarted branch of touchesBegan. The dt==0 sentinel in update() then produces a correct dt=0 on the first post-transition frame instead of a possibly multi-second dt from the stale anchor. Future refactor that moves the lastUpdateTime write inside the guard can no longer teleport the penguin on restart.

title: Snowball in-flight acceleration: faster arrival behind baseZAccel knob, closed-form flight time, fairness invariants
description:
# Snowball In-Flight Acceleration — faster arrival, physically consistent

## Context

Mina's device feedback: snowballs reach the player too slowly and should *gain*
velocity on the way in ("come faster to the user and increase velocity with
correct physical boundaries"). Today each ball flies at a constant per-volley
`zSpeed` (338–546 pt/s at `paceScale 1.3`; 1.65–2.66 s flights over
`zMonster = 900`). "Correct physical boundaries" = every place that assumes
constant speed must stay consistent: the aim-lead intercept math, the
dodgeability fairness invariant (EncounterPaceTests), the hit-window sweep, and
the flight-progress visuals (ball height arc + shadow).

Constraint: the simulator embargo is still on (Mina's call, re-confirmed), so
the gate is compile-only (`xcodebuild build-for-testing`, generic destination);
the new/updated unit tests must compile now and will execute under the
existing verification-debt bead `penguinslide-x06`. Mina feel-tests on device.

## Approach

Add a constant per-ball depth acceleration, with one new pace-coupled knob and
a closed-form flight-time helper so *nothing* keeps assuming constant speed.
Balls launch at the current speeds (telegraph reaction window preserved) and
rush as they approach — arrival ~20–30% sooner, arrival velocity ~40–55%
higher, all tunable from one knob.

### 1. Tuning knob — `PenguinSlide/Tuning.swift`

In the pace block (next to `baseZSpeedStart/End`):

- `static let baseZAccel: CGFloat = 120` — depth acceleration (pt/s²) at pace 1.0.
- `static let zAccel: CGFloat = baseZAccel * paceScale * paceScale` — derived;
  acceleration is distance/time², so the one-knob pace contract scales it by
  paceScale² (time compression squared). Document this in the comment; the
  ONE-KNOB test in EncounterPaceTests gets a matching assertion.

At pace 1.3: zAccel ≈ 203. Fastest ball (v0 546): flight 900 pt in ≈ 1.36 s
(was 1.65), arriving ≈ 776 pt/s. Slowest (v0 338): ≈ 1.75 s (was 2.66).

### 2. Closed-form flight time — `PenguinSlide/Encounter/Snowball.swift`

New pure function beside `snowballAimWorldX` (unit-tested):

```swift
/// Exact time for a ball to cover `spawnZ` from speed v0 under constant
/// accel a: solves spawnZ = v0·t + a·t²/2 (a == 0 falls back to spawnZ/v0).
func snowballFlightTime(spawnZ: CGFloat, zSpeed: CGFloat, zAccel: CGFloat) -> TimeInterval
```

(quadratic root: `(-v0 + sqrt(v0² + 2·a·z)) / a`, guarding a ≈ 0 and v0 ≥ 0.)

### 3. Ball state + integration — `Snowball.swift`, `SnowMonsterEncounterSystem.swift`

- `Snowball` struct: `let zSpeed` → `var zSpeed`; add `let zAccel: CGFloat`.
- `VolleyPlan` gains `zAccel` (default `Tuning.Encounter.zAccel`), threaded
  through `volleyPlan(...)` like `zSpeed`; the DEBUG `TestVolleyOverrides`
  launch-arg parser gains an optional `accel:` field (default = knob) so the
  gyu.22 hermetic XCUI config stays expressive.
- `spawnSnowball`: store `zAccel`, and compute the aim lead with the EXACT
  accelerated flight time: `flightTime: snowballFlightTime(spawnZ:…, zSpeed:…, zAccel:…)`
  — this keeps the intercept prediction correct (boundary #1).
- `updateProjectiles` (line ~842): semi-implicit Euler, matching the repo's
  manual-integration doctrine:
  `ball.zSpeed += ball.zAccel * dtF; ball.z -= ball.zSpeed * dtF`.
  The hit sweep already handles variable steps (`min(z, previousZ) < depthWindow`
  segment overlap) — no change (boundary #2).
- Flight-progress visuals (`snowballFlightProgress = 1 − z/spawnZ`, ball height
  arc, shadow scale/alpha): UNCHANGED — they're position-based, so they stay
  geometrically correct; in wall-clock time they now rush near arrival, which
  is exactly the wanted read. Add one comment documenting this (boundary #3).

### 4. Fairness invariant — `PenguinSlideTests/EncounterPaceTests.swift` (boundary #4)

- ONE-KNOB test: assert `zAccel == baseZAccel * paceScale²`.
- `testFastestBallIsDodgeableFromRestOnGentlestTiltSetting` and the corridor
  test: replace `flightTime = zMonster / zSpeedEnd` with
  `snowballFlightTime(spawnZ: zMonster, zSpeed: zSpeedEnd, zAccel: zAccel)` —
  the worst case is now the accelerated fastest ball. `worstCaseClearance`
  formula stays valid (drift is constant-lateral; budget = driftVxMax × actual
  flight time). Keep the ≥40%-spare assertion — it is the floor that says
  "dodgeable from rest at the gentlest tilt setting"; if it fails when x06
  runs, `baseZAccel` comes down, never the test.
- New pure tests in `SnowballSystemTests` (or a small new case):
  (a) `snowballFlightTime` quadratic vs a == 0 fallback;
  (b) integration: a ball stepped at 60 Hz with accel crosses z = 0 within
  ~1 frame of the closed-form time (ties integrator to the math the aim and
  fairness tests use).

### 5. README

Add `baseZAccel` row to the "Where to tweak difficulty" table.

## Files

- `PenguinSlide/Tuning.swift` — knob pair.
- `PenguinSlide/Encounter/Snowball.swift` — struct, flight-time helper, comment.
- `PenguinSlide/Encounter/SnowMonsterEncounterSystem.swift` — plan/overrides/spawn/integration.
- `PenguinSlideTests/EncounterPaceTests.swift`, `PenguinSlideTests/SnowballSystemTests.swift` — invariants.
- `README.md` — knob table row.

## Verification (sim embargo honored)

1. `xcodebuild build-for-testing -project PenguinSlide.xcodeproj -scheme PenguinSlide -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator'` → must report TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED (compiles app + both test bundles, no simulator boot).
2. Note on bead: runtime execution of the pace/flight tests lands under `penguinslide-x06` when the sim frees up.
3. Mina device pass (`./run-device.sh` when she's ready): balls should launch at familiar speed and visibly rush in the last third; volley should still be dodgeable at default tilt response.
4. Beads/mail: track as a new P1 bead under the epic (sibling of fr7), close on the compile gate with the deferred-runtime marker, report in its mail thread.

title: Replace userData["gravity"] with typed FallingNode subclass
description:
## Background

Icicles (post-detach) and shards both have a per-instance gravity stored as `node.userData?["gravity"] as? CGFloat`. The integration loop in `integrateCustomGravity` looks them up by this string key. Problems:
1. Typo-unsafe: `node.userData?["graivty"]` would silently no-op (cast returns nil → skipped → icicle floats).
2. Allocates an NSMutableDictionary per node.
3. Conceptually wrong — "this node has its own gravity" is a type property, not a runtime tag.

## Fix

Add `PenguinSlide/FallingNode.swift`:

```swift
import SpriteKit

/// Sprite node that integrates its own gravity per frame via
/// the host scene's gravity-integration step. Used for icicles
/// (post-detach) and for shatter shards. Setting `gravity = 0`
/// effectively pauses gravity for that node.
final class FallingNode: SKSpriteNode {
    var gravity: CGFloat = 0
}
```

### Spawn sites
- **Icicles**: spawn as `FallingNode(texture:size:)`. Leave `gravity = 0` during warning. Set `gravity = perIcicleGravity` in the detach SKAction.run block.
- **Shards**: spawn as `FallingNode(texture:)`. Set `gravity = Tuning.sceneGravity` (or `Tuning.Icicle.sceneGravity` after Bead 7).

### Integration loop
```swift
private func integrateCustomGravity(dt: TimeInterval) {
    for child in children {
        guard let node = child as? FallingNode, node.gravity > 0,
              let body = node.physicsBody else { continue }
        body.velocity.dy -= node.gravity * CGFloat(dt)
    }
}
```

### Landing check
Replace `userData?["gravity"] != nil` with `node.gravity > 0` (after a `(node as? FallingNode)` cast).

## Acceptance

1. Zero `userData["gravity"]` references remain.
2. Adding/removing gravity-driven nodes is type-safe.
3. No behavior change.
4. Compile clean.

## Files
- PenguinSlide/FallingNode.swift (NEW)
- PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift (or IcicleSystem.swift after Bead 6)
- PenguinSlide.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj — register the new file

Same type-safety goal achieved via composition rather than the SKSpriteNode subclass originally proposed. See GameScene.swift:143-148, :606, :714, :639-676. if score > best {

title: Font fallback (don't hardcode AvenirNext)
description:
## Background

`SKLabelNode(fontNamed: "AvenirNext-Bold")` (and Heavy, Medium) is used at multiple sites. If Apple ships an iOS that drops Avenir Next, every label silently falls back to Helvetica with no warning. The fallback is acceptable visually but worth being intentional.

## Fix

Add a helper:

title: Skill-based scoring (close-call bonus and dodge combo)
description:
## Background

Current scoring: `score = Int(elapsed * 10)`. Pure survival time, identical for a player who hugged the edge vs. one who threaded the needle. README claims dodging is the core loop, but the score is decoupled from skill.

## Goals
1. Reward close-call dodges (icicle lands near the penguin without hitting it).
2. Combo multiplier for consecutive close calls within a short window.
3. Visible feedback (HUD combo counter when combo > 1).

## Algorithm

On icicle SHATTER event (already wired via `checkIcicleLandings`):
```swift
let dx = abs(landingPoint.x - penguin.position.x)
if dx < Tuning.Score.closeCallRadius {
    let bonus = Int(Tuning.Score.closeCallBase * comboMultiplier)
    score += bonus
    timeOfLastDodge = elapsed
    combo += 1
    hud.showCombo(combo, bonus: bonus)
}
```

Per-frame: decay combo if no close call within `Tuning.Score.comboWindow`:
```swift
if elapsed - timeOfLastDodge > Tuning.Score.comboWindow {
    combo = 0
    hud.hideCombo()
}
```

## New Tuning constants
(Inside `Tuning.Score` sub-enum if Bead 7 done; otherwise flat:)
- `closeCallRadius: CGFloat = 60` — distance from penguin x for the icicle landing to count
- `closeCallBase: Int = 50` — base bonus before multiplier
- `comboWindow: TimeInterval = 2.5` — seconds between close calls to keep the streak
- `comboMaxMultiplier: CGFloat = 5.0` — cap so it doesn't run away

## HUD additions
- Combo counter appears below score label when combo >= 2, fades after `comboWindow` of inactivity.
- Optional: bonus popup text floats up from the landing point on close call.

## Acceptance
1. Standing-still survival no longer grows score as fast as active-dodging play.
2. Combo HUD appears and increments correctly.
3. Combo resets when player gets clipped (game over) or misses the window.
4. Tuning constants are documented in README.

## Files
- PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift (or IcicleSystem.swift + HUDController.swift after Bead 6)
- README.md — add Score section to tuning table

## Notes
Scope-creep risk. Implement close-call bonus FIRST as a single commit; combo multiplier as a follow-up. Don't bundle.

title: Rename Cat struct to Category
description:
## Background

The bitmask collection for physics categories is named `Cat` (with members `Cat.penguin`, `Cat.icicle`, `Cat.shard`). Reads ambiguously — sounds like cat (animal) or cathode (ray) more than "category." No length benefit, no domain reason to abbreviate.

## Fix

Rename `Cat` → `Category`. Update all references in any file that uses it.

If done BEFORE Bead penguinslide-6 (extraction): only `PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift` is affected.

If done AFTER Bead #6: also affects `IcicleSystem.swift`, `Penguin.swift`, and any other extracted file referencing categories.

Recommend doing this BEFORE Bead #6 to minimize file-touch surface.

## Acceptance

1. Zero `Cat.` references remain.
2. No behavior change.
3. Compile clean.
